pairs.why: A's chunky, smoothly rendered rope with soft broad highlights matches the scarf and fan, while B has finer fiber texture and thin, wiry loops, the too-textured look the lessons penalize.
A has the soft, chunky, smooth finish of the real cards, while B's thin rope, odd figure-eight build and rough fiber texture read as less like the game.
B has more believable construction (boiler bands, piston rods, rivets, proper cab and tender) like the detailed bus, while A is a more simplified toy with a slab front and heavy yellow stripes.
A is built like a real locomotive, with a grille cowcatcher, side rods and a coal tender, in clean smooth rendering, while B uses a flat slab for the front.
B's bright red-and-black engine has a proper cowcatcher, cab and spoked wheels, giving the clean, saturated, well-built look of the bus and coaster, while A has a blocky slab front.
B's locomotive has more real mechanical structure and a finish closer to the bus, while A is a chunkier, toy-like simplification with a slab front.
A reads as a properly built engine, with a grille cowcatcher, connecting rods and a tender, smoothly rendered like the real cards, while B's slab front looks toy-like.
A's colorful, well-built side-view engine (red cab, red cowcatcher, spoked wheels) matches the polish and saturation of the real vehicles better than B's blocky slab-fronted engine.
